title: The Solar System
seo_title: Grade 5 Science: The Solar System Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: The solar system has the Sun, eight planets and their moons, and smaller bodies; planets differ in size, distance from the Sun and the time they take to orbit it. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 5, Quarter 4: Earth and Space)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 4: Earth and Space): the Sun and the planets, distances and scale, years and orbits, the Moon and satellites and telescopes. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: The Earth rotates once a day and revolves once a year.
body_html:
How to think about it

The solar system is the Sun and everything that orbits it: eight planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune), dwarf planets, moons, asteroids and comets. The four inner planets are rocky; the four outer planets are giants made mostly of gas and ice.

The Earth rotates on its axis every 24 hours and revolves around the Sun every 365 days. The Moon orbits the Earth about every 29 days. Telescopes and space probes collect light and radio waves from space; PAGASA runs an astronomical observatory and planetariums show the night sky.

Example

Which planet is closest to the Sun?

The smallest inner planet

Answer: Mercury

Example

Why does a planet far from the Sun have a long year?

Its orbit is bigger.

Answer: it has a longer path around the Sun

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the Sun is a planet.
  • Thinking the planets are close together.
  • Mixing up rotation and revolution.

faq.q: Why are telescopes built on high mountains?
faq.a: The air is thin, dry and far from city lights, so the night sky is clear and dark.
With robot rovers and orbiting spacecraft, because the trip is too long and dangerous for people so far.

items.q: Which phase of the Moon comes just before the waning crescent?
items.e: Waxing means growing; waning means shrinking.

items.q: Sheila sketches the Moon from the Northern Hemisphere. Which phase is shown?
items.e: Waxing phases are lit on the right; waning phases are lit on the left.

items.q: Which direction does the Sun appear to rise?
items.e: Earth spins from west to east.

items.q: Tonight Arnel sees a waning crescent. About which phase will Arnel see about two weeks later?
items.e: The cycle is new → waxing crescent → first quarter → waxing gibbous → full → waning gibbous → third quarter → waning crescent, about 29.5 days.

items.q: What happens in a solar eclipse?
c: The Moon passes between the Sun and Earth and blocks the Sun.
items.e: Never look at the Sun, even during an eclipse.

items.q: What causes ocean tides?

items.e: Two high tides a day happen in most places.

items.q: What is space junk?
c: old satellites and pieces of rockets orbiting Earth
items.e: It can hit working satellites.

items.q: A person stands at the North Pole. Which arrow shows the direction that Earth's gravity pulls on the person?
items.e: Gravity pulls toward the center of Earth, so arrow B (pointing into the globe) is “down” for this person.

items.q: What is a satellite?
c: an object that orbits a planet
items.e: The Moon is a natural satellite.

items.q: What is a light-year?
c: the distance light travels in one year
the time it takes to see a star
items.e: A light-year is a distance: about 9.5 trillion kilometers.

items.q: Why can't we see stars during the day?
c: Stars move away during the day.
The sun's bright light hides their dimmer light.
items.e: The stars are still there. Sunlight scattered in the sky outshines them.

items.q: Why does the sun look much brighter than other stars?
c: It is much closer to Earth than any other star.
It is the only star that gives off light.
Other stars are turned off in the day.
items.e: The sun is about 150 million km away. The next closest star is about 270,000 times farther.

items.q: A person stands at a place on the right side of Earth. Which arrow shows the direction that Earth's gravity pulls on the person?
items.e: Gravity pulls toward the center of Earth, so arrow D (pointing into the globe) is “down” for this person.

items.q: A person stands at a place on the right side of Earth. Which arrow shows the direction that Earth's gravity pulls on the person?
items.e: Gravity pulls toward the center of Earth, so arrow C (pointing into the globe) is “down” for this person.

items.q: Why do astronauts wear space suits on a spacewalk?
c: to give air and protect them from extreme temperatures and radiation
items.e: Space has no air to breathe.

items.q: A person stands at the South Pole. Which arrow shows the direction that Earth's gravity pulls on the person?
items.e: Gravity pulls toward the center of Earth, so arrow A (pointing into the globe) is “down” for this person.

items.q: Why do astronauts exercise every day on the space station?
c: Without Earth's pull, their muscles and bones get weaker.
items.e: Exercise keeps them healthy.

items.q: What is the sun?
items.e: The sun is a star, like the stars you see at night.

items.q: A star looks very dim from Earth. Which could be true?
c: It must not give off light.
It may be very far away.
It must be smaller than a house.
items.e: Distance can make even a very bright star look dim.

items.q: A person stands at the North Pole. Which arrow shows the direction that Earth's gravity pulls on the person?
items.e: Gravity pulls toward the center of Earth, so arrow D (pointing into the globe) is “down” for this person.

items.q: Which instrument lets you see craters on the Moon from your backyard?
items.e: Telescopes make faraway things look closer.

items.q: Why are rockets launched with huge amounts of fuel?
c: They need a lot of thrust to escape Earth's gravity.
Because space is full of air
items.e: Leaving Earth takes a lot of energy.

items.q: Which statement about stars is true?
c: Stars are closer than the moon.
Stars are holes in the sky.
All stars are smaller than Earth.
Many stars are as big as or bigger than the sun.
items.e: Stars look like tiny dots only because they are so far away.

items.q: How did many Indigenous Peoples use the night sky?
c: to tell time, find directions and mark seasons
items.e: Star knowledge is passed down through stories.

items.q: Which object in the sky is a star?
items.e: The moon and planets reflect sunlight. The sun makes its own light.

items.q: Which is closest to Earth?
items.e: The sun is our closest star.
